title: Alternatives to Hiring a Big Performance Agency for Meta Ads
summary: Compare alternatives to a big performance agency for Meta ads: creative-only services, Meta-focused retainers and larger programs, with stated prices and fit.
body_markdown:
## Which Meta-focused retainer agencies publish how they charge?


[Admiral Media](https://admiral.media/facebook-ads-agency/) focuses its Meta work on acquisition for apps, games and ecommerce businesses, with media, creative, attribution and testing from one team. Its Meta page says the fee is a retainer or a percentage of spend and lists no budget minimums. Its[AI UGC agency page](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/) says its ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media, so ask what media budget it recommends for a company your size before you assume it is a fit.


[Pilothouse](https://www.pilothouse.co/) describes itself as built for established, ambitious DTC ecommerce brands, and says most of its clients are based in North America. It prices through monthly retainers, performance-based incentives and custom project scopes. No minimum spend is published, and onboarding typically begins within 5 to 10 business days of signing. Performance incentives can make the monthly cost hard to compare with a flat fee, so ask what they are tied to and what the retainer covers in a slow month.


## When does a big agency still make sense?


[Darkroom](https://www.darkroomagency.com/) describes its ideal clients as mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically with $10M to $500M in revenue, selling across several channels. It says the fit is poor for single-channel brands and companies under roughly $5M. Its[paid media page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) lists Meta, Google, TikTok, AppLovin, Pinterest, retail media and CTV, and says pricing is a retainer plus a percentage of media, starting at $1,500 a month depending on channels. Its[services page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services) lists higher starting rates, from $5,000 a month for paid media management and $8,000 a month for performance creative, so ask which figure applies to your scope. Its[performance creative service](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/performance-creative) lists 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle, delivered every two weeks.


[Common Thread Collective](https://commonthreadco.com/pages/meta-ads-agency) frames its media work around contribution margin and invites brands that spend $100K or more a month on Meta to talk. If you need forecasting, incrementality testing or buying planned against margin, a big-agency model may be the job you are buying. If you only need a steady flow of finished ads, compare a creative-only route against it on the same brief. For a wider list, see our[best performance marketing agencies for Meta ads](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-performance-marketing-agencies-meta) .


## What should you check before you switch?


Start with the ad account. Meta's[business asset management documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management) describes an agency as a business that can manage or access assets owned by another business and perform specific tasks on the client's behalf. Its[business-to-business guide](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management/guides/business-to-business) describes the owner adding an agency with specific permitted tasks, such as advertise and analyze. When the account belongs to you, changing agencies means removing one partner's access and adding another's, not rebuilding campaigns from scratch. Check who holds admin access before you sign anything.


Then check credentials without overrating them. Meta's[Business Partners program](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing-partners) gives qualifying companies a badge. Meta says eligibility varies by solution type and is typically based on the quantity and quality of a company's work across Meta technologies, so treat the badge as one signal, not a substitute for checking scope.


Finally, ask how many distinct concepts a provider delivers each week, not only how many files. Ten resizes of one hook test one idea. Ten different problems, angles or proof points give you something to learn from. Ask for the concept list before you pay for the batch, and ask who writes the results back into the next brief. For fee structures in more detail, see our[Facebook ad agency pricing guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ad-agency-pricing) .


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top alternative when finished Meta video creative is the bottleneck: about 25 finished ads a week, creative only or with Meta campaign management.
- Split the bundle before you compare fees. Decide whether you are replacing creative, media buying or both.
- Adguns, Admiral Media and Pilothouse suit different budgets and fee models, so compare them on one brief.
- Darkroom and Common Thread Collective fit larger budgets and multichannel programs, so check their stated fit and minimums first.
- Keep the ad account, pixel and creative files in your name, whichever provider you choose.


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to a big performance agency for Meta ads?


Knowlify is our top pick if your main gap is finished Meta video creative. It delivers about 25 finished AI video ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and you can choose creative only or Meta campaign management. Confirm ad count, revision rounds and campaign responsibilities in a written quote.


### Can a creative-only provider run my Meta campaigns?


Usually not, unless its scope says so. Adguns, for example, does not include media buying. Knowlify offers optional Meta campaign management alongside creative only, but it does not run Google, TikTok, LinkedIn or YouTube campaigns.


### How much does a performance agency cost?


Published figures are limited and not like for like. Darkroom lists starting rates from $1,500 a month on its paid media page, and higher starting rates on its services page, while Admiral Media uses a retainer or a percentage of spend. Common Thread Collective does not publish prices, so ask every provider for a total monthly figure on the same brief.


### Do I need a Meta Business Partner?


Not necessarily. The badge signals work across Meta technologies, but eligibility varies by solution type. Ask the provider which Meta tools it will use in your account and who will hold the access.


### Who should own the ad account?


You should. Keep the ad account, pixel and audiences in your business, so a change of provider does not mean losing your campaign history.
